Taoism. Taoism, also spelled Daoism, is a philosophical and spiritual tradition originating in China that emphasizes harmony with the Tao, "the Way"—the underlying principle of the universe—through non-action, or wu wei, simplicity, and alignment with natural forces. Developing from early philosophical texts like the Tao Te Ching attributed to Laozi, it became both a philosophical worldview and an organized religion with deities, rituals, and monasteries, profoundly influencing East Asian thought and spirituality.

The Tao is conceptualized as an ineffable, eternal, unchanging force underlying all existence. It cannot be named or fully understood through language, only experienced through living in harmony with it. Wu wei, or non-action, is a core concept meaning acting in accordance with the Tao naturally, without force or resistance. It advocates spontaneity, flexibility, and acceptance of the natural course of events.

The Tao Te Ching, attributed to Laozi and likely compiled in the fourth or third century BCE, is the foundational text of philosophical Taoism. It presents paradoxical wisdom about the Way through short, poetic passages. Yin and Yang represent complementary opposites in Taoist cosmology. Yin is passive, dark, and feminine while yang is active, light, and masculine. Together they generate and balance all phenomena, and neither dominates as harmony requires both.

Organized religious Taoism developed later, from the second century CE onward, incorporating folk deities, ancestor veneration, and ritual practices. It created a priesthood and monastic traditions alongside philosophical Taoism. Taoist practice traditionally includes meditation, breath work called qigong, and martial arts like tai chi, aimed at aligning the self with the Tao and cultivating longevity or spiritual immortality.

Taoism influenced Zen Buddhism, Korean Shamanism, and Japanese Shinto, spreading throughout East Asia. It offers a counterbalance to the hierarchical, duty-focused ethics of Confucianism within Chinese civilization.
